stories.title: Student AI Research Earns International Recognition
stories.thumbnailAlt: One of the most rewarding aspects of being a faculty member in the College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing is seeing student capstone projects evolve into impactful research. We are excited to share that three Master of Science in Data Analytics capstone projects have been further developed into research papers on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning for human health.

stories.title: Faculty Secure $300K DOE Grant to Advance AI-Driven Scientific Discovery
stories.thumbnailAlt: The College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing is excited to announce that Dr. Tanja Horn, Professor of Physics, and Dr. Dominick Rizk, Assistant Professor of Computer Science, recently secured $300,000 in funding from the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) for their research project titled, “AI-Driven Expedited Discovery and Background Separation for Petabyte-Scale Streaming Readout.”

stories.title: J. Steven Brown Appointed Dean of the College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing
stories.thumbnailAlt: The College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing of The Catholic University of America is pleased to announce that, effective July 1, 2026, J. Steven Brown, Ph.D., has been appointed Dean of the College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing. Bringing deep institutional knowledge and an unwavering commitment to students, faculty, and research, Dean Brown is well positioned to build on the College’s recent momentum and lead it into its next chapter of growth.

stories.title: Tanja Horn Awarded $750,000 NSF Grant to Advance Nuclear Physics Research and AI Innovation
stories.thumbnailAlt: Dr. Tanja Horn, professor in the Department of Physics at The Catholic University of America, has been awarded a $750,000 grant from the National Science Foundation (NSF) to support her research in experimental nuclear physics. The project, titled "Studies of Pion and Kaon Structure and AI to Expedite Science Output," will advance the understanding of the fundamental building blocks of matter while integrating artificial intelligence to accelerate scientific discovery.

stories.title: Mechanical Engineering Faculty Receive NIH and ITHC Grants for Sepsis Research
stories.thumbnailAlt: Xiaolong Luo, Ph.D., and Zhaoyang Wang, Ph.D., both faculty members in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, have been awarded a $596,250 grant from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) for their research project, “A Rapid Antibiotic Susceptibility Testing (AST) Platform Using Multiplex Static Gradients.”

stories.title: CEPC Students Support NASA’s Artemis II Mission
stories.thumbnailAlt: Melissa Kane and Carina Alden, both enrolled in the Applied Space Weather Research (ASWR) master’s program, currently serve as full-time space weather analysts with NASA’s Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office (M2M SWAO). As analysts, they contributed to the recent Artemis II mission through continuous space weather analysis in support of mission control operations.

stories.title: Multimodal AI Lab Wins Global Recognition at SAFE Challenge
stories.thumbnailAlt: The Multimodal AI Lab (MAIL) at the College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing earned international recognition at the SAFE: Image Edit Detection and Localization Challenge, organized by the Digital Safety Research Institute (DSRI-UL). The lab’s SIGN-MAIL system, developed by graduate researcher Ansar Ali, won first place in five global categories for image manipulation localization and placed third overall, highlighting the strength of the College’s expanding AI research program.

stories.thumbnailAlt: On April 14th, 2025, Hanseok Ko, Ph.D., professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, was installed as the Newton-Bennett Endowed Chair of Engineering. Ko is an expert in artificial intelligence (AI), multimodal signal processing, and intelligent human-computer interfaces.

stories.title: School of Engineering Hosts Third Annual Senior Design Night
stories.thumbnailAlt: On March 31, 2025, the School of Engineering hosted the third annual Senior Design Night in Heritage Hall, Father O’Connell Hall. stories.title: Mechanical Engineering Seniors Win NASA Research Competition

stories.title: Civil and Environmental Engineering Students Compete at ASCE Student Symposium
stories.thumbnailAlt: On March 28th-29th, undergraduate students from the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering competed at the combined 2025 Mid-Atlantic East and West American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) Student Symposium at Pennsylvania State University, in State College, Pennsylvania. The symposia is one of the core foundations of student involvement within the American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE), as a means to highlight each university’s and college’s ingenuity.

stories.title: Data Analytics Alumnus Develops Application for Urban Navigation
stories.thumbnailAlt: David Schneider, M.S. 2024, a recent alumnus in the data analytics graduate program, developed a mobile application that helps users navigate and explore Washington, D.C. using the public transportation systems.

stories.title: School of Engineering Offers Artificial Intelligence Workshops
stories.thumbnailAlt: This past fall, the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science began offering free artificial intelligence (AI) workshops for Catholic University students. These workshops included group discussion and tutoring sessions on AI, ranging from introductory-level instruction to more advanced concepts and applications.

stories.title: School of Engineering Hosts the 16th Annual Senior Design Day for the Class of 2024
stories.thumbnailAlt: On Monday, April 29th, 2024, the School of Engineering hosted the 16th Annual Senior Design Day in the Pryzbyla Center Great Rooms. Each senior design group had the opportunity to present their final capstone project to the faculty, staff, family members, and students who attended. In addition, the projects were judged by several School of Engineering faculty members; students competed for the following awards: Best Presentation, Best Poster, and Best Overall Project.

stories.title: School of Engineering Students and Faculty Win Awards at University Research Day 2024
stories.thumbnailAlt: This year’s University Research Day took place on April 17th, 2024. School of Engineering students and faculty attended the event, presenting their research projects to members of the Catholic University community. This annual event highlights the research and innovation currently being conducted at the university and serves as a platform to celebrate the academic contributions regularly made by our students and faculty.

stories.title: School of Engineering Hosts the Spring 2024 Senior Design Night
School of Engineering Doctoral Student Wins D.C. Council of Engineering and Architectural Societies Annual Paper Competition
stories.thumbnailAlt: Every year, the District of Columbia Council of Engineering and Architectural Societies (DCCEAS) hosts an annual competition as part of Engineering Week, where students from 18 universities across the National Capital Region showcase their research papers and compete for the Best Paper Award at both the undergraduate and graduate level. This year’s graduate winner is Catholic University, Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. candidate, Razan Bahabri.

stories.title: Researchers at the School of Engineering Develop Novel Tissue Chip to Study Oral Mucositis
stories.thumbnailAlt: Researchers in the School of Engineering at The Catholic University of America have created a novel tissue chip to study oral mucositis, a painful condition involving extensive mouth ulcers, in cancer patients treated with chemo- and radiotherapy.

stories.title: Two School of Engineering Seniors Accepted Into Naval Flight School
stories.thumbnailAlt: Ryan Walczak and Miles Shealy are seniors at The Catholic University of America’s School of Engineering. They are both midshipmen in the Naval Reserve Officer Training Corps preparing to be officers in the United States Navy. Both have a passion for engineering and aviation and were recently accepted into Naval Flight School, a prestigious program that prepares naval officers to serve as military pilots. They are also good friends who met at Catholic University.

stories.title: School of Engineering Hosts High School STEM Symposium for Second Year
stories.thumbnailAlt: On Saturday, February 24th, the Catholic University of America hosted the 61st Greater Washington, D.C. Region Junior Science & Humanities Symposium. This was the university’s second year in a row hosting the event, which provides high school students with the opportunity to showcase their research, compete for scholarships, and develop skills for further pursuits in STEM.

stories.title: Career Development at the School of Engineering Networking Night and Informational Interviewing Event
stories.thumbnailAlt: On February 6th, 2024, the Center for Academic and Career Success hosted the Spring 2024 School of Engineering Networking Night and Informational Interviewing Event in Maloney Hall. Employers, students, and faculty spent the evening discussing career opportunities, jobs and internships, and professional development.
